svg.title: Figure 4.3: Delayed-choice quantum eraser, records and conditional detection patterns
svg.desc: Panel A: a sequence of events in a representative delayed-choice quantum-eraser arrangement: correlated signal-idler preparation, signal detection and permanent record, later idler measurement, and comparison of two records. Panel B: smooth unconditioned signal-detector distribution. Panels C and D: complementary conditional interference patterns after sorting the earlier signal detections by the later idler records in an eraser basis. The weighted sum of these two conditional distributions equals the unconditioned distribution. No earlier event is changed.
svg.text: Delayed-choice quantum eraser: records and conditional patterns
Later measurement records can sort earlier detections; they do not alter the unsorted data
A. A delayed-choice arrangement: two records, one complete history
Arrows denote particle propagation (solid) or comparison of existing records (dashed)—not backward causation.
Eraser-basis example with equally weighted outcomes:
½ P(x | +) + ½ P(x | −) = P(x) — the original unsorted distribution
Delayed-choice quantum eraser: records and conditional detection patterns.
In a delayed-choice arrangement, the signal is recorded before the idler measurement. Sorting the fixed earlier detections by later idler records can reveal
complementary interference patterns in selected subsets. Their weighted sum reproduces the unchanged unsorted distribution; no earlier event is modified.
